Senses.Explanation: The recorded formula "outside the eon." The Chan corpus uses it as a productive modifier and location in sayings and verse: "spring light beyond the eon" (劫外春光), "the spring beyond the eon returns and the ten thousand things wither" (劫外春回萬物枯), and "the true lineage beyond the eon" (劫外真宗). It is paired explicitly with the time before buddhas and patriarchs were born: "before buddhas and patriarchs were born, outside the empty eon" (佛祖未生空劫外). It also enters public address as a demand to "take responsibility beyond the eon" (於劫外承當), contrasted in the same question with meeting now (而今相見, "meeting at present"). The corpus thus bends chronological language into a recurrent Chan register for the sayings, activity, spring, and lineage it places outside or before measured epochs.

Senses.Explanation: The aeon-ending fire blazes (劫火洞然) names the conflagration said to destroy the great chiliocosm. In Longmen's recorded sayings, an unnamed monk uses the phrase to ask whether ‘this’ too is destroyed; Longmen replies with ‘golden color inside a black-lacquer bucket.’ Yuanwu Keqin writes that even while this fire blazes there is ‘no change’ (初無變異). Zhongji Kezun's verse uses the same blazing scene in the line ‘when the aeon-ending fire blazes, it is fitting to boil tea’ (劫火洞然宜煑茗). These are different uses of one image, not different lexical senses.

Senses.Explanation: To sift sand and select gold is to distinguish a sought item from surrounding lookalikes or waste. Chan speakers turn that sorting scene into appraisal of discernment: an unnamed monk opposes fish-eyes mixed with pearls to Muchen Daomin's sifting, Yuanwu Keqin uses it for two elders examining a case, Guantao Daqi credits Yunmen's quick eye and hand, and Jifei Ruyi applies it to finding rare trust. Senses.Explanation: Do not take this the wrong way warns that the conclusion a listener is drawing from the preceding words does not follow. Yushan Shangsi gives the warning after a monk reduces the exchange to the least trace of a formulation, and Linye Tongqi gives it after a monk announces that the Linji house has been renewed. Dahui Zonggao warns against equating silence with the condition before one's parents were born. Zhaozhou Congshen rejects calculation from borrowed sayings, while Bao'en Huiming states four possible readings of his replies and rejects all four with the same warning.
